newsitem.title: USA: Vermont lawmakers eye $20 million budget surplus.
newsitem.headline: Vermont lawmakers eye $20 million budget surplus.

text.p: Vermont lawmakers still might have to deal with property tax reform and get a budget approved, but they do have one thing going for them -- a $20 million surplus in tax receipts for the first quarter of 1997.

The surplus, far more than the tax department had anticipated, could help finance property tax reform, or be applied to any of a number of social programs. The windfall also could be used to start a rainy day fund for future fiscal emergencies.
"This is excellent news," said Kathy Hoyt, Governor Dean's longtime Chief of Staff, who last week became Dean's Administration Secretary. "It's evidence that our programs are succeeding."
